# Room Warden

> Room Warden is hotel operations software. It puts housekeeping, live room status, airport shuttle pickups, maintenance tickets, guest room requests, guest feedback and events in one web app. It runs alongside any property management system (PMS) and needs no PMS integration.

Key facts:
- Built for select-service and airport hotels, usable by any property.
- Also tracks parking and park and fly, lost and found, shift notes and other front desk lists.
- Automates daily, weekly and monthly reports, including reports for audits, from what staff log, ready to open in Excel. Every entry is time-stamped, and summaries export for bookkeeping and accounting.
- Guests call the hotel for a shuttle pickup and get a text with the pickup spot and time, plus a heads-up when the driver is close; no guest app.
- Staff use it in a web browser on any phone, tablet or computer.
- Every staff member gets their own admin-issued login with per-user permissions.
- Hosted on dedicated servers with a failover server and regular backups.
- Pricing is quoted per property; book a demo at https://roomwarden.com/#contact.

## Blog

- [Hotel housekeeping room status codes, explained](https://roomwarden.com/blog/housekeeping-room-status-codes): What VC, VD, OC, OOO, OOS and the other hotel room status codes mean, how they differ, and why live status updates matter for the front desk.
- [How to run a hotel shuttle without the radio](https://roomwarden.com/blog/hotel-shuttle-text-requests): A simpler way to run an airport hotel shuttle: log pickups when guests call, keep the driver and front desk on one screen, and text guests the pickup spot and time.
- [What your PMS doesn't cover (and what hotels use instead)](https://roomwarden.com/blog/what-your-pms-doesnt-cover): A property management system handles reservations and billing, but daily hotel operations like shuttles, maintenance and guest requests often live on radios, whiteboards and group chats.
- [How to write a front desk shift log the next shift will actually read](https://roomwarden.com/blog/front-desk-shift-log): What to put in a hotel front desk shift log, what to leave out, and how to hand over between shifts so open issues don't get lost overnight.
- [How to track park and fly cars at an airport hotel](https://roomwarden.com/blog/park-and-fly-tracking): What to record when a guest leaves their car for park and fly, how to keep the lot count right, and how to avoid the 'where's my car' call at 1am.
- [How to track hotel maintenance requests so nothing gets lost](https://roomwarden.com/blog/hotel-maintenance-requests): A simple process for hotel maintenance requests: log every issue with a room and a description, assign it, and only close it when maintenance confirms the fix.
- [How to handle guest room requests without losing any](https://roomwarden.com/blog/guest-room-requests): Extra towels, a crib, more pillows. How hotels can log guest requests, send them to the houseman or housekeeping, and confirm they were delivered.
- [A simple lost and found process for hotels](https://roomwarden.com/blog/hotel-lost-and-found): How to log, store and return items guests leave behind: what to record, how to label items, and how to answer the 'did you find my charger' call quickly.
